title: Crypto Payments Complete Guide
subtitle: Master Crypto Payments from Consumer Transactions to Enterprise Treasury

intro.title: Introduction to Crypto Payments
intro.content:
Cryptocurrency is evolving from a speculative asset to a real medium of exchange. While early crypto payments were slow and expensive, modern payment infrastructure makes crypto transactions faster and cheaper than traditional payment systems.

This guide covers the entire crypto payment ecosystem: from buying your first crypto with a credit card, to accepting payments as a merchant, to managing enterprise payroll with streaming payments. You'll learn about the technologies making crypto payments practical, the tools available today, and how businesses are already using crypto to move money globally.

payment_rails.title: Crypto Payment Rails
payment_rails.content:
Not all blockchains are suitable for payments. Bitcoin's base layer processes only 7 transactions per second with fees that can reach $50+ during congestion. Ethereum isn't much better during peak usage.

Modern payment infrastructure uses specialized blockchains and layer 2 networks designed for high throughput and low costs. Understanding these payment rails is essential for choosing the right solution.

stablecoins.title: Stablecoins: The Payment Standard
stablecoins.content:
Stablecoins are the foundation of crypto payments. Nobody wants to price their coffee in Bitcoin when it might swing 10% before they finish drinking it.

Why stablecoins dominate payments:

  • Price stability: $1 USDC today = $1 USDC tomorrow
  • Instant settlement: Transfers settle in seconds, not 3-5 business days
  • Global reach: Send $100 or $1,000,000 anywhere with the same ease
  • Programmability: Automate recurring payments, splits, and escrow

Leading payment stablecoins:

  • USDC (Circle): Fully reserved, regulated, most trusted for business
  • USDT (Tether): Highest liquidity, widely accepted globally
  • PYUSD (PayPal): PayPal-issued, growing merchant adoption
  • EURe (Monerium): Regulated Euro stablecoin for European markets

layer2.title: Layer 2 Networks for Payments
layer2.content:
Layer 2 networks inherit Ethereum's security while offering dramatically lower fees and faster confirmation times. This makes them ideal for everyday payments.

Popular payment L2s:

  • Base: Coinbase's L2, designed for consumer crypto adoption. Fees ~$0.01 per transaction
  • Arbitrum: Largest L2 by TVL, extensive DeFi ecosystem for payment integrations
  • Optimism: Fast finality, popular for payroll and recurring payments
  • Polygon: High throughput, widely supported by payment providers

Real-world example: A coffee shop using Coinbase Commerce on Base pays $0.01 per transaction versus $5-15 on Ethereum mainnet. With 100 daily transactions, that's $1 vs $500-1,500 in daily fees.

bitcoin_lightning.title: Bitcoin Lightning Network
bitcoin_lightning.content:
The Lightning Network is a layer 2 payment protocol built on Bitcoin. It enables instant, near-zero-fee Bitcoin payments by creating payment channels between users.

How it works:

  1. Open a payment channel by locking Bitcoin on-chain
  2. Make unlimited instant payments off-chain through the Lightning Network
  3. Close the channel to settle final balance on-chain

Lightning adoption:

  • El Salvador uses Lightning for official Bitcoin payments
  • Strike, Cash App, and other apps support Lightning
  • Growing merchant adoption in emerging markets

Lightning is particularly valuable in regions with expensive traditional banking infrastructure.

merchant_solutions.title: Merchant Payment Solutions
merchant_solutions.content: Accepting crypto payments as a merchant requires different tools than consumer wallets. Merchant solutions handle invoicing, payment tracking, accounting integration, and compliance.

payment_gateways.title: Crypto Payment Gateways
payment_gateways.content:
Payment gateways are the crypto equivalent of Stripe or PayPal—they handle the complexity of accepting crypto so merchants don't have to.

Coinbase Commerce:

  • Free to use, 1% fee for instant conversions to fiat
  • Accepts Bitcoin, Ethereum, USDC, and more
  • E-commerce plugins for Shopify, WooCommerce, etc.
  • Non-custodial—merchants receive funds directly

BitPay:

  • One of the oldest crypto payment processors (since 2011)
  • Settlement in crypto or fiat
  • Supports major cryptocurrencies
  • Compliance tools for tax reporting

NOWPayments:

  • Supports 300+ cryptocurrencies
  • Lower fees than traditional gateways
  • Auto-conversion to preferred currency
  • API for custom integrations

Integration example: Add crypto checkout to your Shopify store in under 10 minutes using Coinbase Commerce plugin. No coding required.

pos_systems.title: Point of Sale (POS) Systems
pos_systems.content:
Physical retail stores need point-of-sale solutions that work like traditional credit card terminals but for crypto.

Features of crypto POS systems:

  • QR code generation for customer payments
  • Real-time price conversion (display in local currency)
  • Instant payment confirmation
  • Integration with existing cash register systems
  • Automatic tax calculation

Benefits for merchants:

  • Lower fees: 0.5-1% vs 2-3% for credit cards
  • No chargebacks: Crypto payments are final
  • Instant settlement: Funds available immediately
  • Global customers: Accept payments from tourists without currency conversion fees

invoicing.title: Crypto Invoicing
invoicing.content:
B2B payments need professional invoicing tools. Crypto invoicing platforms create payment requests with due dates, line items, and automatic payment tracking.

Request Network:

  • Decentralized invoicing protocol
  • Create invoices with crypto or fiat amounts
  • Automatic payment detection
  • Export for accounting software (QuickBooks, Xero)

Utila:

  • Crypto invoicing and payroll
  • Multi-currency support
  • Team collaboration features
  • Compliance documentation

Use case: A freelance designer invoices a client for $5,000. The client pays in USDC on Arbitrum. Request Network automatically detects the payment, marks the invoice paid, and exports the record to the designer's accounting software.

payroll_streaming.title: Payroll & Streaming Payments
payroll_streaming.content: One of crypto's most innovative features is programmable money. Streaming payments let you pay salaries by the second, creating new compensation models impossible with traditional finance.

streaming_payments.title: Streaming Payments Explained
streaming_payments.content:
Traditional payroll: Work 2 weeks, get paid on Friday.
Streaming payments: Get paid continuously as you work.

How streaming payments work:

  1. Employer deposits funds into a streaming contract
  2. Funds flow continuously to employee's wallet (e.g., $50,000/year = $1.58 per second)
  3. Employee can withdraw at any time
  4. Stream automatically stops when funds run out or contract ends

Superfluid:

  • Real-time money streaming protocol
  • Create continuous payment streams with one transaction
  • Used by DAOs and crypto-native companies
  • Supports Ethereum, Polygon, Optimism, Arbitrum, Base

Sablier:

  • Token vesting and streaming
  • Linear, cliff, and custom vesting schedules
  • Used for employee compensation, grants, and token unlocks
  • NFT-based streams (streams are transferable)

LlamaPay:

  • Simple streaming interface
  • Lower gas costs through optimized contracts
  • Ideal for DAO contributor payments

payroll_management.title: Crypto Payroll Management
payroll_management.content:
Managing payroll for remote, global teams is challenging with traditional banking. Crypto payroll solves this by treating international and domestic payments identically.

Utopia Labs:

  • Payroll platform for DAOs and crypto companies
  • Pay contractors globally in crypto or fiat
  • Automated tax calculations
  • Compliance documentation for different jurisdictions

Parcel:

  • Batch payment tool for DAOs
  • Pay multiple recipients in one transaction
  • CSV import for bulk payments
  • Integration with Gnosis Safe for treasury management

Real-world savings: A company with 20 international contractors spends $50-75 per international wire transfer. That's $1,000-1,500 monthly just in wire fees. With crypto payroll: $20-50 total monthly fees, regardless of employee location.

revenue_sharing.title: Revenue Sharing & Payment Splits
revenue_sharing.content:
Crypto makes it easy to split payments automatically among multiple recipients—perfect for partnerships, royalties, and revenue sharing.

0xSplits:

  • Trustless payment splitting protocol
  • Define percentage splits (e.g., 70% founder, 20% investor, 10% charity)
  • All incoming payments automatically split
  • Immutable or updatable splits
  • Zero fees (just gas)

Reveel:

  • Revenue distribution platform
  • Create payment waterfalls (pay A first, then B, then split)
  • Time-based distribution changes
  • Analytics dashboard

Use case: Three co-founders set up a 0xSplits contract: 40/30/30. They point all company revenue (merchant payments, investments, grants) to this address. Every payment automatically splits correctly, eliminating manual accounting and trust issues.

fiat_ramps.title: Fiat On-Ramps & Off-Ramps
fiat_ramps.content: The bridge between traditional and crypto finance. On-ramps let you buy crypto with fiat; off-ramps let you convert crypto back to fiat.

onramps.title: Fiat On-Ramps
onramps.content:
On-ramps are how most people enter crypto. They accept credit cards, bank transfers, and local payment methods.

MoonPay:

  • Supports 160+ countries
  • Credit/debit card and bank transfer
  • Buy directly into your wallet
  • Embedded in MetaMask, Rainbow, and other wallets
  • Fees: 3.5-4.5% for cards, lower for bank transfer

Transak:

  • Global coverage with local payment methods
  • Lower fees in many regions
  • White-label solution for dApps
  • Compliance built-in (KYC/AML)

Ramp:

  • Non-custodial on-ramp
  • Buy crypto that goes directly to your wallet
  • SDK for dApp integration
  • Support for Apple Pay and Google Pay

Choosing an on-ramp: Compare fees carefully—they vary significantly by payment method and region. Card purchases are fastest but most expensive (3-5%). Bank transfers are cheapest (0.5-1%) but take 1-3 days.

offramps.title: Fiat Off-Ramps
offramps.content:
Converting crypto back to fiat is often harder than buying crypto. Off-ramps specialize in this direction.

Spritz:

  • Pay bills directly with crypto
  • Connect bank accounts and credit cards
  • Auto-pay setup for recurring bills
  • No need to manually convert and withdraw

Monerium:

  • Regulated e-money institution in Europe
  • Issue on-chain EUR (EURe) backed 1:1 by bank deposits
  • Redeem EURe directly to IBAN bank account
  • Institutional grade compliance

Use case: A freelancer receives $10,000 USDC payment on Polygon. Using Spritz, they can pay their $2,000 rent directly from USDC without first converting to USD, sending to bank, then paying landlord. Saves time and fees.

crypto_cards.title: Crypto Debit Cards
crypto_cards.content:
Crypto debit cards let you spend crypto anywhere Visa or Mastercard is accepted. They auto-convert crypto to fiat at point of sale.

Gnosis Pay:

  • Self-custody Visa card
  • Spend directly from your Gnosis Safe
  • No exchange intermediary
  • Available in Europe

How they work:

  1. Load your card wallet with USDC or other crypto
  2. Swipe at any merchant accepting Visa/Mastercard
  3. Card provider auto-converts crypto to local fiat
  4. Merchant receives fiat as normal

Benefits:

  • Spend crypto without merchant adoption
  • Earn DeFi yields on card balance before spending
  • Self-custody (for some cards)

Considerations:

  • Each purchase is a taxable event in most jurisdictions
  • Conversion fees (typically 0.5-2%)
  • Not all cards are available in all regions

remittances.title: Remittances & Cross-Border Payments
remittances.content: Crypto shines brightest in cross-border payments. Traditional international transfers are slow (3-5 days), expensive (5-10% fees), and require banking infrastructure.

use_cases.title: Remittance Use Cases
use_cases.content:
Migrant worker remittances:

Worldwide, migrants send $700+ billion annually to their home countries. Traditional services like Western Union charge 5-10% in fees. Crypto remittances can cost 0.5-2%.

Example flow:

  1. Worker in USA buys USDC on Coinbase ($100 - $1 fee = $99 USDC)
  2. Send USDC on Polygon to family in Philippines ($0.01 transaction fee)
  3. Family converts USDC to Philippine Peso on local exchange ($99 - 1% fee = $98 received)

Traditional wire: $100 - $7 fee - $3 receiving bank fee = $90 received
Crypto: $100 - $1 - $0.01 - $1 = $98 received

That's $8 more received (8% better) and instant instead of 3-5 days.

Business payments:

  • Pay international suppliers without wire fees
  • Receive payments from global customers
  • Treasury management across borders

advantages.title: Why Crypto Wins for Cross-Border Payments
advantages.content:
Speed: Crypto transactions settle in seconds to minutes. SWIFT transfers take 3-5 business days. During weekends and holidays, SWIFT stops. Crypto doesn't.

Cost: Wire transfers: $25-50 per transaction. Crypto on L2: $0.01-1.00. For large amounts, the difference is even more dramatic.

Access: 1.7 billion people globally are unbanked but have smartphones. They can receive crypto without a bank account.

Transparency: Track payments in real-time on blockchain explorers. With wires, money disappears into the banking system for days.

Always on: Send money at 3am on Sunday. Try that with a bank.

Challenges:

  • Crypto literacy required on both ends
  • Exchange rate volatility (solved by stablecoins)
  • Last-mile fiat conversion still needed in many places
  • Regulatory uncertainty in some jurisdictions

treasury.title: Treasury Management
treasury.content: For organizations holding significant crypto, professional treasury management tools are essential for security and operational efficiency.

multi_sig.title: Multi-Signature Wallets
multi_sig.content:
Never store company funds in a single-signature wallet. Multi-sig requires multiple approvers for transactions, eliminating single points of failure.

Gnosis Safe (Safe):

  • Industry standard for multi-sig wallets
  • M-of-N signature schemes (e.g., 3-of-5 signers required)
  • Support for any ERC-20 token and NFTs
  • Available on 10+ networks

Setting up treasury multi-sig:

  1. Choose number of signers (5-7 for large organizations)
  2. Set signature threshold (usually 50-60% of signers)
  3. Add trusted signers from different parts of organization
  4. Document recovery procedures
  5. Test with small amount first

Coinshift:

  • Built on top of Gnosis Safe
  • Adds treasury analytics and reporting
  • Scheduled payments and automation
  • Role-based access control
  • Accounting export

batch_payments.title: Batch Payments
batch_payments.content:
Paying multiple recipients individually wastes time and gas fees. Batch payment tools combine many payments into one transaction.

Parcel:

  • Upload CSV of recipients and amounts
  • One transaction pays everyone
  • Save 80-95% on gas fees
  • Integrated with Safe for approval workflow

Example: A DAO needs to pay 50 contributors. Individual transactions: 50 × $2 gas = $100 in fees. Batch payment: $5 in fees. Plus, recipients get paid simultaneously instead of one at a time.

Use cases:

  • Monthly contributor payroll
  • Airdrop distributions
  • Investor dividend payments
  • Multi-party settlements

compliance_tax.title: Compliance & Tax Considerations
compliance_tax.content: Crypto payments create new compliance and tax obligations. Ignoring these can lead to serious legal and financial consequences.

kyc_aml.title: KYC/AML Requirements
kyc_aml.content:
Most payment providers require Know Your Customer (KYC) and Anti-Money Laundering (AML) compliance.

When KYC is required:

  • Fiat on-ramps and off-ramps (always)
  • Payment processors serving merchants (usually)
  • Large transaction volumes (varies by jurisdiction)

Sardine:

  • Compliance and fraud prevention platform
  • Instant KYC verification
  • Transaction monitoring
  • Risk scoring

For merchants:

  • Document customer information for large transactions
  • Monitor for suspicious activity
  • Maintain transaction records
  • File required reports (CTR, SAR in USA)

tax_reporting.title: Tax Reporting for Crypto Payments
tax_reporting.content:
In most jurisdictions, receiving crypto payments is a taxable event. The complexity varies by use case.

For businesses accepting crypto:

  • Record fair market value in local currency at time of receipt
  • Report as revenue like any other payment
  • Track cost basis for future sales
  • Document all transactions for audits

For employees paid in crypto:

  • Crypto salary is taxed as ordinary income
  • Value determined at time of receipt
  • Later sale creates additional capital gains/losses

For contractors:

  • Crypto payments are self-employment income
  • Track carefully for estimated tax payments
  • Deduct business expenses as usual

Tools:

  • Request Network generates tax-ready invoices
  • Accounting integrations with QuickBooks, Xero
  • Crypto tax software: Koinly, CoinTracker, TokenTax

best_practices.title: Payment Best Practices
best_practices.content:
For merchants:

  1. Use established payment processors, don't roll your own
  2. Accept stablecoins to avoid volatility
  3. Auto-convert to fiat if you can't hold crypto
  4. Clearly display crypto payment option at checkout
  5. Provide instant payment confirmation

For organizations:

  1. Use multi-sig for all treasury funds (minimum 3-of-5)
  2. Keep hot wallet balances low, most funds in cold storage
  3. Document all payment approvers and processes
  4. Use batch payments for efficiency
  5. Maintain detailed transaction records
  6. Work with crypto-savvy accountants

For individuals:

  1. Start with small test transactions
  2. Verify recipient addresses carefully (they can't be reversed)
  3. Use ENS names or address book to avoid typos
  4. Keep records of all crypto income and payments
  5. Understand tax implications before accepting crypto salary

Security checklist:

  • ✓ Hardware wallet for large amounts
  • ✓ Multi-sig for organizational funds
  • ✓ Test transactions with small amounts first
  • ✓ Verify smart contract addresses
  • ✓ Use payment requests, not manual address entry
  • ✓ Monitor addresses for unexpected transactions

payment_rail.definition: The underlying infrastructure for moving money. In crypto, this includes blockchains (Ethereum, Bitcoin), layer 2 networks (Arbitrum, Optimism), and sidechains (Polygon) that process payment transactions.

streaming_payment.definition: A continuous flow of money from sender to recipient over time, often measured per second. Enabled by smart contracts that release funds continuously rather than in discrete paychecks.

invoice.definition: A payment request document with details like amount, due date, and line items. Crypto invoices can be paid directly with cryptocurrency and automatically marked as paid when the blockchain transaction is detected.

remittance.definition: Money sent from one location to another, typically by migrant workers to family in their home country. Crypto significantly reduces remittance costs compared to traditional services.

pos.definition: A system where retail transactions occur, like a cash register or payment terminal. Crypto POS systems generate QR codes for customers to scan and pay with cryptocurrency.

merchant.definition: A business that sells goods or services. Crypto merchant solutions let businesses accept cryptocurrency payments alongside traditional payment methods.

payment_gateway.definition: A service that handles payment processing for merchants, similar to how Stripe processes credit cards. Crypto payment gateways handle cryptocurrency payments and optionally convert to fiat.

fiat_onramp.definition: A service that converts traditional currency (fiat) into cryptocurrency. On-ramps accept credit cards, bank transfers, or local payment methods and deliver crypto to your wallet.

fiat_offramp.definition: A service that converts cryptocurrency back into traditional currency. Off-ramps withdraw crypto from your wallet and deposit fiat into your bank account or pay your bills directly.

payment_token.definition: A cryptocurrency designed for use as a medium of exchange. Stablecoins like USDC and USDT are the most common payment tokens due to their stable value.
